venue: The Coca-Cola Roxy, The Battery Atlanta, GA
blurb: Trippie Redd is coming to the Coca-Cola Roxy on Monday the 24th, right before Thanksgiving week heats up. If you're in that mid-20s to early-30s range and have been following his catalog, this is a good excuse to get out before the holiday chaos takes over. The Roxy is one of the better mid-size venues in Atlanta and The Battery makes the whole night easy, with parking and plenty of options for dinner before the show. Check the Know Before You Go page on the Roxy's site before you head out.
scoring_notes: Trippie Redd skews younger than the median Perimeter audience (age 38), but the audience has enough young professionals in the mix to make this relevant. The Battery location is squarely in the coverage zone. Uniqueness is solid — a specific artist, one night only. Demographic fit is the main question mark; this is a pick for the younger end of the Perimeter readership.

event_name: The Nutcracker — Georgia Metropolitan Dance Theatre
venue: Jennie T. Anderson Theatre, Marietta, GA
blurb: Thanksgiving afternoon, the family is around, and you need something to do with the next few hours before the second round of food. Georgia Metropolitan Dance Theatre's production of The Nutcracker is a genuinely nice option — live dance, holiday atmosphere, the kind of thing that actually holds a family's attention across ages. The Jennie T. Anderson Theatre in Marietta is a solid venue and this is Thanksgiving weekend, so if you're going, don't wait on tickets.
scoring_notes: The Nutcracker runs every year so uniqueness is moderate, but the Thanksgiving timing and family-friendly format make it relevant for this audience's mix of young families and empty nesters. Slight distance from Perimeter core but within range. Good fit as a Thanksgiving day activity. Not a standout pick on its own but fills a real use case for the audience.

venue: C. Ellet's, The Battery Atlanta, GA
blurb: Saturday morning with nowhere to be, a live jazz duo, Southern fried chicken, and a mimosa in hand at C. Ellet's. This is a weekly thing but that doesn't make it less worth doing, especially heading into Thanksgiving week when a slow, good brunch at The Battery sounds about right. The jazz duo plays from 11 to 3 every Saturday and Sunday. Make a reservation, go with someone you like talking to, and take your time.
scoring_notes: Recurring weekly event, so uniqueness is low. That said, it's a legitimate experience at a well-known Battery restaurant that fits the adult-leaning Perimeter audience well. Good fallback option. The timing right before Thanksgiving makes it contextually relevant as a 'treat yourself' pick heading into the holiday. Strong demographic fit for empty nesters and young professionals.

blurb: It's a free outdoor festival in Roswell with gourmet food trucks, craft drinks, live music, DJ sets, and college football on big screens all afternoon. The Fall and Flavor Festival at You42 Studios is a genuinely easy yes for a Saturday where you want to get out of the house but don't want to plan too hard. Bring the family, bring friends, eat something interesting, and catch whatever game is on. It's right at the top of the Perimeter coverage area and it won't cost you a thing to walk in.
scoring_notes: Free entry is appealing but not the main draw — the combination of food trucks, live music, and game day screens makes it genuinely multi-use for this audience. Roswell is on the northern edge of the coverage area but reachable. Good fit for young families and young professionals. Uniqueness is moderate since outdoor food festivals are common, but the timing right before Thanksgiving week gives it seasonal relevance.

venue: Park Bench, The Battery Atlanta, GA
blurb: Black Friday night, no cover, two pianists playing off each other and off the crowd, right at The Battery. This is exactly what you want after a full day of family. Dueling Pianos at Park Bench is the kind of show where the setlist depends on who's in the room and what they're asking for — it's loud, it's fun, and it moves fast. General seating fills up, so grab a table reservation if you want to actually sit down. Walk in otherwise and see what happens. Either way, it's a good night.
scoring_notes: The Battery is a natural Perimeter destination. No-cover entry plays well for spontaneous post-Thanksgiving plans. Adult-skewing event fits the audience well. Uniqueness is moderate since Dueling Pianos runs regularly, but the holiday timing and 'Holiday Kickoff' framing make this iteration relevant. Strong audience match for the young professionals and empty nesters in the mix.

blurb: If you grew up with Journey on the radio, this one is worth the drive to Marietta. DEPARTURE has been doing this for 18 years and they're considered the best Journey tribute band in the country, which isn't a small claim. The lead vocalist matches Steve Perry note for note, everything you hear is played live, and they run through two full sets of the hits. VIP gets you a meet and greet, drink tickets, a signed poster, and a mini concert starting at 6:30. The Strand is a beautiful old theater, it's Black Friday night, and Don't Stop Believin' is going to sound really good right now. Grab your tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Journey's core fanbase maps well to the 38 median age and older end of the Perimeter audience. The Strand is a beloved venue with regional pull. The 18-year track record and national reputation give this credibility beyond a typical tribute act. Black Friday night timing is a genuine selling point. Slight distance from core Perimeter coverage but well within reasonable drive. VIP experience adds a premium tier that works for the $105K HHI.

event_name: BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience at Truist Park
blurb: Black Friday plans just got a serious upgrade. This one is genuinely one-of-a-kind: you and up to five others get a behind-the-scenes tour of the Atlanta Braves clubhouse, batting cages, and dugout, plus the chance to play catch on the field. BLOOPER shows up in full holiday mode, there's a festive photo op, and you walk away with a photo next to the NL East Pennant. If you've got kids who love the Braves, this is not a thing you can replicate on a random Saturday. It's holiday-exclusive, it's inside a stadium most people never see from that angle, and it's the kind of morning that beats another lap around a mall by a mile.
scoring_notes: Truist Park is in the Perimeter audience's backyard. The holiday-exclusive access angle is genuinely unique — this isn't a standard stadium tour. Strong pull for young families and young professionals with kids. The $105K median HHI means ticket price is a non-issue. Uniqueness score is a 10 because behind-the-scenes clubhouse access on a holiday weekend is not something you stumble into.

event_name: 10th Annual Tree Lighting at The Battery Atlanta
blurb: The Battery Atlanta's 10th Annual Tree Lighting is one of those holiday kickoff events that actually delivers on the vibe. Free admission, festive activities, ornament decorating, family photos with oversized holiday props, and giveaways while supplies last. Once the tree goes up, the night keeps going with an outdoor movie on the Plaza Green. Bring blankets, grab a spot, and settle in. The Battery is a fun venue to be in on a holiday night, with plenty of food and drink options around the plaza to make a full evening of it. If you've got family in town for Thanksgiving weekend and are looking for something low-effort and genuinely fun for a mix of ages, this checks the boxes.
scoring_notes: Free events aren't inherently strong picks for a $118K median income audience, but the 10th anniversary, the outdoor movie add-on, and the Thanksgiving weekend timing give it real situational relevance. Skews more family-friendly than adult, which is a slight mismatch for the empty nester portion of East Cobb, but works well for the established families with teens or visiting relatives.

blurb: Thanksgiving weekend and The Nutcracker go together like nothing else, and Georgia Metropolitan Dance Theatre's production at the Jennie T. Anderson Theatre is the local version worth putting on the calendar. GMDT puts their own spin on the classic: a mischievous magician sets the whole story in motion, toy soldiers battle giant mice, and the journey through the Kingdom of Sweets includes dances from around the world. Six performances run across the holiday weekend, so you've got options whether you're hosting family or just looking for something to do with the out-of-town relatives that everyone will actually enjoy. For families with younger kids still in the house, or grandparents visiting for the week, this is a low-effort, high-reward evening out.
scoring_notes: East Cobb skews toward families with teens and empty nesters, so this hits better for the subset with younger grandkids or relatives visiting for Thanksgiving than it does for the core audience. The Nutcracker is not unique, but GMDT's specific production with a local spin and holiday weekend timing gives it real relevance. Multiple performances over Thanksgiving weekend are a practical plus.

event_name: Movies at The Strand: Home Alone (1990)
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: Home Alone on the big screen at The Strand, the night before Thanksgiving. If that's not a tradition worth starting, what is? The Strand's Movies at The Strand series pairs classic films with a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ, so you're getting more than just a movie. You're getting an event. Kevin McCallister, two bumbling burglars, and an organ concert to warm things up before the chaos starts. Bring the family, bring whoever's already in town for the holiday, and make an easy Tuesday night into something everyone actually remembers. The Strand in Marietta is a beautiful old venue and it's the right place to watch a movie that's been around for 36 years and still holds up completely.
scoring_notes: The timing is the whole selling point: night before Thanksgiving, with family already gathering. Home Alone hits nostalgia for the 42-median-age crowd, and the live organ pre-show adds a uniqueness factor that a typical movie night doesn't have. East Cobb families with teens or college kids home for break are the core target here.

event_name: Behind the Cider: A Guided Tasting & Tour
blurb: Eight ciders, a behind-the-scenes production tour, and a full pint to finish, all led by Chloe, the cidermaker who actually makes the stuff. Atlanta Hard Cider's guided tasting is a Saturday afternoon well spent, and at $25 a ticket it's a STEAL for what you're getting. This isn't a pour-and-move-on flight at a bar. You hear the process, see the production area, ask real questions, and walk out with a new appreciation for something you've probably been ordering without thinking twice about. Ages 21+, limited tickets, and the venue is right in Marietta. If you've never visited Atlanta Hard Cider, this is the best possible first visit.
scoring_notes: Adults-only, educational, local, and affordable for this income bracket. The 'meet the maker' format appeals to East Cobb's educated, curious demographic. Limited tickets add a mild urgency factor. Good adult skew, relevant for couples and friend groups. Not a blockbuster event, but a genuinely good fit for this newsletter.

venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: If you grew up with Journey on the radio, Departure is the real deal. In their 18th year together, they're the most respected Journey tribute band in the country, and they play everything live with no pre-recorded tracks. Lead vocalist Brian Williams nails Steve Perry's range in a way that actually holds up in a real theater. The show runs two full sets with an intermission, so this is a proper night out, not a quick bar set. The VIP package gets you a private pre-show mini-concert, early seating, two drink tickets, and a signed poster. The Strand is a beautiful venue, Saturday night before Thanksgiving weekend wraps up, and Don't Stop Believin' live in Marietta? Hard to say no to that.
scoring_notes: Journey's core fanbase is squarely in the 40-55 age range, which lines up with East Cobb's median age of 42. The Strand is a beloved local venue. The VIP option appeals to this income bracket. Tribute bands aren't unique by nature, but Departure's reputation and the theater setting elevate it. Strong audience match for both couples nights out and friend groups.

blurb: Five private homes in one of Marietta's most storied neighborhoods, all decorated for the holidays, all open for one evening. The Marietta Pilgrimage Christmas Home Tour has been a tradition in this community for years, and it draws the kind of crowd that actually appreciates a beautifully restored historic home. You're not just walking through staged interiors; you're seeing how real Marietta families celebrate the season in houses with real history behind them. Historic churches, museums, and other landmark buildings round out the tour. Tickets are $40 in advance, and online sales close December 3rd at 4pm, so don't sit on this one. Proceeds support Cobb Landmarks & Historical Society and Visit Marietta. It's a genuinely lovely way to kick off December.
scoring_notes: 78% homeownership rate and high education level in East Cobb means this audience cares about historic preservation, home design, and community tradition. The $40 ticket is a non-issue at $118K median income. Strong empty nester and established family appeal. Annual event but each year features different homes, so it's not a 'do it anytime' experience.

event_name: Not a Hot Toddy 2026: Marietta's 7th Annual Bartending Competition
blurb: Some of Marietta's best bartenders go head-to-head with cold-weather cocktails, and you're the judge. The Third Door's Not a Hot Toddy competition is back for its 7th year, and your ticket covers dinner from a local food truck, two full-sized cocktails, tastings of all four competing cocktails, and raffle tickets for prizes. You also get a vote for the People's Choice Award, so your opinion actually matters here. And this year they're debuting Marietta Misers & Misfits, a holiday pop-up inspired by nostalgic Christmas classics with a mischievous twist. Ticket holders get first access. This is a genuinely fun adults night out in downtown Marietta, and with Thanksgiving week behind you and December just getting started, the timing couldn't be better.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's $118K median income household treats a cocktail competition dinner ticket as an easy yes. The event skews adult, which fits both the established families (kids are teens or older) and empty nesters in this audience. The 7th annual run signals it's a real, well-organized event. The debut of the holiday pop-up adds a novelty hook that makes this year's edition feel special even for returning attendees.

venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb: Professor Brian Cox is one of the most compelling science communicators alive, and he's bringing his most ambitious live show yet to Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre this Saturday. Emergence covers cosmology, biology, philosophy, and history, presented across massive LED screens with custom music, film, and lighting. Cox built this show alongside scientists, musicians, and filmmakers because he wanted it to feel like more than a lecture. It's designed to leave you thinking about something you hadn't considered before, whether you're a science nerd or just someone who likes to walk out of an event feeling like the world got a little bigger. This is a rare stop. If you've got a curious teenager at home or a partner who'd actually enjoy something different for once, this is worth your Thanksgiving weekend.
scoring_notes: East Cobb is 65% college-educated with a median income of $118K. Brian Cox draws exactly that audience. The show's interdisciplinary scope (science, philosophy, music, art) gives it cross-household appeal, and the fact that it's at Cobb Energy makes it genuinely local. High uniqueness: Cox doesn't tour constantly and this production sounds like a one-of-a-kind touring show.
